moments.title: The Mart opens
moments.text: Marshall Field & Co. opened its huge wholesale market on the north bank of the river, pulling 13 warehouses under one roof. With about 4 million square feet, it was the largest building in the world.

moments.title: Joseph Kennedy buys it
moments.text: With the Depression and the war having hurt wholesale trade, Field's sold the building to a group led by Joseph P. Kennedy for far less than it cost to build.

moments.title: The Kennedys sell
moments.text: After more than 50 years, the Kennedy family sold the Mart to Vornado Realty Trust as part of a larger deal.

moments.title: Art on theMART lights up
moments.text: Projectors across the river began throwing digital art onto 2.5 acres of the Mart's river wall, billed as the largest permanent digital art projection in the world.

moments.title: Today: offices, showrooms and night shows
moments.text: The Mart holds offices and design showrooms, and Art on theMART plays on its river wall on many nights.

sources.title: Art On theMART to Launch September 29, 2018 (City of Chicago)

checked.notes: Opening May 5, 1930, Marshall Field & Co. as builder, about 4 million sq ft, Kennedy purchase 1945 and Vornado sale Jan 1998 confirmed (Wikipedia, Chicago Architecture Center, Encyclopedia of Chicago). The Kennedy price is disputed ($12.5 million or $16 million), so no figure is given. Art on theMART launched Sept 29, 2018 (City of Chicago). 'Largest building until the Pentagon' per Wikipedia.
